summary: Lists characters that can't begin an unquoted scalar (`[] {} > | * & ! % # ` @ ,`) and recommends quoting values starting with `? : -`. Notes stricter rules in flow collections, quoting literal booleans like "yes" and "False", and quoting float-like version numbers such as "1.0".
questions: Why did my value yes turn into true?
How do I keep a version number like 1.0 as a string in requirements.yml?
Which characters can't start an unquoted YAML value?
Why is my partially quoted path invalid YAML?
Do I need quotes inside { } flow mappings?

answer_card.title: More YAML gotchas: special characters, booleans, versions
answer_card.answer_md:
- Partial quoting is invalid: `foo: "E:\\path\\"rest\\of\\path`.
- These can't be the first character of an unquoted scalar: ``[] {} > | * & ! % # ` @ ,``. Also quote values starting with `? : -`, since parsers differ.
- Flow collections are stricter: `{ key: "you { should [ use , quotes here" }`.
- To keep a literal boolean-looking string, quote it:
  ```yaml
  non_boolean: "yes"
  other_string: "False"
  ```
- Float-looking strings like `1.0` are converted to floats; quote version numbers:
  ```yaml
  version: "1.0"
  ```
